afniblurimage.oneliner: This algorithm performs image smoothing using AFNI's blurImage code
afniblurimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js afniblurimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The image to smooth
  -m --mask [s]   An optional mask image
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --sigma [n]   The gaussian kernel standard deviation fwhm mm (default=1), range=0:16
  --usemask [s]   If true only mask within a region (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

approximatefield.oneliner: Calculates the displacement field for a given transformation for a given image.
approximatefield.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js approximatefield [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   Load the displacement field image to approximate
  -o --output <s>   Stores the fitted transformation to the input displacement field
  --lambda [n]   Extra regularization smoothness term weight (default=0.1), range=0:1
  --tolerance [n]   Fitting to tolerance (default=0.001)
  --windowsize [n]   Fitting quality (default=2), range=1:2
  --inverse [s]   if true approximate inverse displacement field (default=false)
  --spacing [n]   The control point spacing of the output grid transform (default=25), range=2:50
  --optimization [s]   Optimization Method (default=ConjugateGradient), values=[HillClimb,GradientDescent,ConjugateGradient]
  --stepsize [n]   Step size for gradient computation (default=0.5), range=0.125:4
  --levels [n]   Number of levels in multiresolution optimization (default=2), range=1:4
  --iterations [n]   Number of iterations (per level and step) (default=20), range=1:32
  --resolution [n]   Factor to reduce the resolution prior to registration (default=2), range=1:5
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)
  --steps [n]   Number of steps in multiresolution optimization (default=1), range=1:4

backprojectimage.oneliner: This algorithm performs back projection from 2D to 3D. This is meant for mapping 2D optical images to 3D MRI images
backprojectimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js backprojectimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The image to be back-projected
  -t --target <s>   The image to backproject to
  -x --xform [s]   The transformation to reslice the 2d image before backprojecting
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --flip [s]   It true project along the increasing axis (default=false)
  --flipy [s]   It true flip the vertical  axis (default=false)
  --axis [s]   Which axis to project along ('x', 'y', 'z', 'auto') (default=y), values=[x,y,z,auto]
  --threshold [n]   The intensity threshold to detect background in shaded projection (default=0.5), range=0:1000
  --window [n]   Number of voxels to average in 'average' or 'project' mode (default=3), range=1:40
  --reduce [n]   Factor to reduce the resolution of the 2D image by (default=2), range=1:8
  --interpolation [n]   Which type of interpolation to use (3 = cubic, 1 = linear, 0 = nearest-neighbor) when reducing (default=1), values=[0,1,3]
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

bidsconversion.oneliner: This module converts raw DICOM data into NIFTI form using dcm2niix, then formats it to BIDS specifications
bidsconversion.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js bidsconversion [options]

Options:
  --logoutput [s]   log file
  --inputdirectory [s]   Input directory for the DICOM conversion (default=)
  --outputdirectory [s]   Output directory for the DICOM conversion. Optional, saves in /tmp if not specified (default=/var/folders/dx/zx3mlpkn3nv1xlyf_7_1t_g5qqzmfk/T)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

binarythresholdimage.oneliner: This element will threshold an image and create a binary mask
binarythresholdimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js binarythresholdimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output mask
  --low [n]   The threshold below which values will be zeroed (default=1)
  --high [n]   The value above which values will be zeroed (default=1000)
  --inval [n]   The value of the binary mask (default=1), range=1:100
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

bisserver.oneliner: This module runs the BioImageSuite Web WebSocker Based FileServer
bisserver.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js bisserver [options]

Options:
  --logoutput [s]   log file
  --portno [n]   Port number (default=24000), range=24000:24999
  --readonly [s]   Whether or not the server should accept requests to write files (default=false)
  --insecure [s]   Whether or not the server requires a password (use with extreme care) (default=false)
  --proxyport [n]   If enabled, creates a proxy server mirroring http://bisweb.yale.edu/local (use with care) Use -1 to disable (default=0), range=0:32767
  --createconfig [s]   print sample config file and exit (default=false)
  --tmpdir [s]   Location of the Temp Directory (default=)
  --ipaddr [s]   USE WITH EXTREME CARE -- if used this allow remote access (maybe) (default=localhost)
  --config [s]   Location of the Configuration File (default=)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

blankimage.oneliner: This algorithm performs image blanking, i.e. zeros values outside the specified region. It is similar to crop but maintains the original image dimensions.
blankimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js blankimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --i0 [n]   The Start along the i axis. (default=0)
  --i1 [n]   The End along the i axis. (default=10001)
  --j0 [n]   The Start along the j axis. (default=0)
  --j1 [n]   The End along the j axis. (default=10001)
  --k0 [n]   The Start along the k axis. (default=0)
  --k1 [n]   The End along the k axis. (default=10001)
  --minvalue [s]   If true the blanked output image regions will have value equal to the minimum intensity of the image, instead of zero (default=true)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

butterworthfilter.oneliner: This element will apply a Butterworth Filter to an input matrix
butterworthfilter.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js butterworthfilter [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The input data (matrix) to process. Rows=Frames, Columns=Series.
  -o --output <s>   The output matrix
  --type [s]   What type of filter to apply (low, band, or high) (default=band), values=[low,band,high]
  --low [n]   Lowpass cutoff frequency of filter (in Hertz) (default=0.1), range=0:10
  --high [n]   Highpass cutoff frequency of filter (in Hertz) (default=0.01), range=0:10
  --tr [n]   Data time of repetition (Data TR) (default=1), range=0.01:5
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

butterworthfilterimage.oneliner: This module performs temporal Butterworth filtering to an input image. This is performed separately for each voxel
butterworthfilterimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js butterworthfilterimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --type [s]   What type of filter to apply (low, band, or high) (default=band), values=[low,band,high]
  --low [n]   Lowpass cutoff frequency of filter (in Hertz) (default=0.1), range=0:10
  --high [n]   Highpass cutoff frequency of filter (in Hertz) (default=0.01), range=0:10
  --tr [n]   Data time of repetition (Data TR). If <0.0 use spacing from image header (default=-1), range=-1:5
  --removemean [s]   Remove Mean before high pass filtering (default=true)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

calciumpreprocess.oneliner: This module creates a makefile from a CalciumPreprocess json file. Use --sample true to get an example CalciumPreprocess file
calciumpreprocess.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js calciumpreprocess [options]

Options:
  -m --mask <s>   The image frame to mask with
  -r --refimage <s>   The reference image frame
  -o --output <s>   output script
  --setup [s]   Name of the input setup filename (result of stiching _step1) (default=)
  --odir [s]   Output directory (default=)
  --trimstart [n]   Number of frames to trim from the beginning of each timeseries (default=1)
  --trimend [n]   Number of frames to trim from the end of each timeseries. If a file has 6000 frames and this is specified as 200, then the last frame used will by 5800. (default=-1)
  --sigma [n]   The gaussian kernel standard deviation (either in voxels or mm) (default=1), range=0:8
  --inmm [s]   Determines whether kernel standard deviation (sigma) will be measured in millimeters or voxels (default=true)
  --fwhmax [s]   If true treat kernel in units of full-width-at-half max (FWHM) (not as the actual value of the sigma in the gaussian filter.) (default=false)
  --interpolation [n]   Which type of interpolation to use (3 = cubic, 1 = linear, 0 = nearest-neighbor) (default=1), values=[0,1,3]
  --backgroundvalue [n]   Value to use for outside the image (default=0)
  --res [n]   The amount to downsample the reference by (default=2), range=1:4
  --dff [s]   Computes df/f normalization (default=false)
  --doregress [s]   if true regress out second image from first else just normalization (default=true)
  --dilation [n]   The amount (in voxels) to dilate the mask by (default=0), range=0:5
  --biswebpy [s]   Name of the main python script (else biswebpy) (default=)
  --python [s]   Name of the main python3 executable (default=python3)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

changeimagespacing.oneliner: Changes the image header to have new spacing
changeimagespacing.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js changeimagespacing [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --xsp [n]   Desired voxel spacing in X direction (default=1), range=0.1:10
  --ysp [n]   Desired voxel spacing in Y direction (default=1), range=0.1:10
  --zsp [n]   Desired voxel spacing in the z-direction (default=1), range=0.1:10

circleblankimage.oneliner: This algorithm performs image blanking, i.e. zeros values outside the specified circular region.
circleblankimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js circleblankimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --centeri [n]   The ith coordinate of the center of the circular region to keep (default=128)
  --centerj [n]   The jth coordinate of the center of the circular region to keep (default=128)
  --radius [n]   The radius of the center of the circular region to keep (default=128)
  --minvalue [s]   If true the masked output image regions will have value equal to the minimum intensity of the image, instead of zero (default=true)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

clusterthreshold.oneliner: This element will separate an image into clusters and apply binary thresholding. The image is first thresholded using a threshold. Then it is filtered to remove binary blobs that smaller than the cluster size selected.
clusterthreshold.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js clusterthreshold [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image
  --threshold [n]   The value to threshold at (zero out voxels below threshold) (default=1)
  --size [n]   Size of clusters to form (default=1000), range=2:1000000
  --oneconnected [s]   Whether to use 6 or 26 neighbors (default=true)
  --keeplargest [s]   If true return only largest cluster (default=false)
  --frame [n]   Which frame from the time series to cluster (fourth dimension) (default=0)
  --component [n]   Which component to take a frame from (fifth dimension) (default=0)
  --outclustno [s]   It true the output image is filled with the cluster number instead of the actual image values (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

combineimages.oneliner: Combines two images in different ways. This can be either arithmetic combination (add, subtract, multiply, divide) or combine them by appending one after the other.
combineimages.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js combineimages [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The first input image
  -s --second <s>   The second input image
  -o --output <s>   The combined image
  --mode [s]   Operation to perform, i.e. how to combine the images. (default=add), values=[add,subtract,multiply,divide,append,scaledappend]
  --weight1 [n]   Scalar to multiply image 1 by before operation (default=1), range=-100:100
  --weight2 [n]   Scalar to multiply image 2 by before operation (default=1), range=-100:100
  --outtype [s]   Output Type (default=Float), values=[UChar,Short,Float,Double]
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

computecorrelation.oneliner: Computes the correlation matrix for an input matrix (pairwise) with weights
computecorrelation.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js computecorrelation [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The input data (matrix) to process. Rows=Frames, Columns=Series.
  -w --weight [s]   (Optional). The framewise weight vector
  -o --output <s>   The output matrix
  --zscore [s]   Convert correlations to z-score. (default=true)
  --usejs [s]   Use the pure JS implementation of the algorithm (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

computeglm.oneliner: Calculates the Generalized linear model (GLM) for fMRI data sets
computeglm.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js computeglm [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   Load the image to fit the model to
  -r --regressor [s]   The regressor matrix
  --mask [s]   Load the mask for the input
  -o --output <s>   Output beta map image
  --numtasks [n]   How many of the actual columns in the regressor are actual tasks -- if 0 then all. (default=0), range=0:20
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

computeroi.oneliner: Takes an input time series and ROI map and returns the mean intensity in the roi as a matrix of frames(rows)*roiindex(columns)
computeroi.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js computeroi [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   Load the image (time series) to be averaged into regions
  -r --roi [s]   parcellation/regions of interest to compute signal averages for
  -o --output <s>   The output matrix
  --storecentroids [s]   If true store the centroid of each roi as last three columns (default=false)
  --storevolume [s]   If true output the volumes of the vois instead of the mean value (default=false)
  --usejs [s]   Use the pure JS implementation of the algorithm (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

computeroilarge.oneliner: Takes an input time series and ROI map and returns the mean intensity in the roi as a matrix of frames(rows)*roiindex(columns)
computeroilarge.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js computeroilarge [options]

Options:
  -r --roi [s]   parcellation/regions of interest to compute signal averages for
  -o --output <s>   The output matrix
  --input [s]   This is the input filename (default=)
  --loadall [s]   If true (default=false), load all images first, then process (default=true)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

computevolume.oneliner: Takes an input objectmap and computes the volumes of the various regions
computevolume.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js computevolume [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   Objectmap
  -o --output <s>   The output matrix
  --keepzero [s]   If true store the volume of the background region (0) (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

concatenateimages.oneliner: Concatenates Multiple Images to a single 4D Image
concatenateimages.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js concatenateimages [options]

Options:
  --output [s]   This is the output concatenated series filename (default=)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

cropimage.oneliner: This algorithm performs image cropping in 4 dimensions. Step refers to the sample rate, e.g. step=2 means every second voxel.
cropimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js cropimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --i0 [n]   The Start along the i axis. (default=0), range=-10:200
  --i1 [n]   The End along the i axis. (default=10), range=-10:200
  --di [n]   The Step along the i axis. (default=1), range=-10:200
  --j0 [n]   The Start along the j axis. (default=0), range=-10:200
  --j1 [n]   The End along the j axis. (default=10), range=-10:200
  --dj [n]   The Step along the j axis. (default=1), range=-10:200
  --k0 [n]   The Start along the k axis. (default=0), range=-10:200
  --k1 [n]   The End along the k axis. (default=10), range=-10:200
  --dk [n]   The Step along the k axis. (default=1), range=-10:200
  --t0 [n]   The Start along the t axis. (default=0), range=-10:200
  --t1 [n]   The End along the t axis. (default=10), range=-10:200
  --dt [n]   The Step along the t axis. (default=1), range=-10:200
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

defaceimage.oneliner: This module uses data from the openfmri project to deface an image by first registering it to a template using a linear affine registration.
defaceimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js defaceimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --resolution [n]   Factor to reduce the resolution prior to registration (default=3), range=1:5
  --iterations [n]   Number of iterations (per level) (default=5), range=1:32
  --levels [n]   Number of levels in multiresolution optimization (default=2), range=1:4
  --imagesmoothing [n]   Amount of image smoothing to perform (default=2), range=0:4
  --outputmask [s]   If true output the mask (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

dicomconversion.oneliner: This module converts raw DICOM data into NIFTI form using dcm2niix, then formats it to BIDS specifications
dicomconversion.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js dicomconversion [options]

Options:
  --logoutput [s]   log file
  --inputdirectory [s]   Input directory for the DICOM conversion (default=)
  --outputdirectory [s]   Output directory for the DICOM conversion. Optional, saves in /tmp if not specified (default=)
  --convertbids [s]   Whether or not to format the DCM2NII converted files to BIDS. Optional, defaults to true (default=false)
  --fixpaths [s]   Used by bisserver on windows (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

diffspect.oneliner: Performs diff SPECT Analaysis for Epilepsy
diffspect.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js diffspect [options]

Options:
  -i --ictal <s>   The ictal image
  -r --interictal <s>   The incter-ictal image
  -m --mri [s]   The MRI image
  -o --output <s>   diff SPECT Tmap in Atlas Space
  --output2 [s]   diff SPECT Tmap in Native Space
  --logoutput [s]   log file
  --nonlinear [s]   If true use nonlinear registration (default=false)
  --native [s]   If true output tmap in native space (default=false)

displacementfield.oneliner: Calculates the displacement field for a given transformation for the volume specified by the given image.
displacementfield.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js displacementfield [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   Image that defines the output size
  -x --xform <s>   Load the transformation to compute the displacement field for
  -y --xform2 [s]   The second transformation to combine with first
  -z --xform3 [s]   The third transformation to combine with first and second
  -o --output <s>   Output displacement field image
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

driftcorrectimage.oneliner: Drift Corrects an Image by fitting and removing a polynomial to each voxel time series separately.
driftcorrectimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js driftcorrectimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -w --weight [s]   (Optional). The framewise weight vector
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --order [n]   Which type of drift correction to use (3 = cubic, 2=quadratic, 1 = linear, 0 = remove-mean) (default=3), range=0:3
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

extractframe.oneliner: This element will extract a single frame from a time-series.
extractframe.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js extractframe [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --frame [n]   Which frame in the time series to extract (fourth dimension) (default=0)
  --component [n]   Which component to extract a frame from (fifth dimension) (default=0)
  --usejs [s]   Use the pure JS implementation of the algorithm (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

extractslice.oneliner: This element will extract a slice from a single frame of a time-series.
extractslice.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js extractslice [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --plane [n]   Which plane to extract from the image (0 = Sagittal, 1 = Coronal, 2 = Axial) (default=2), range=0:2, values=[0,1,2]
  --slice [n]   Which slice in the given plane to extract (default=-1)
  --frame [n]   Which frame in the input image to extract (fourth dimension) (default=0)
  --component [n]   Which component to extract a frame from (fifth dimension) (default=0)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

flipimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js flipimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   input
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --flipi [s]   Determines if the i-axis (x) will be flipped (default=false)
  --flipj [s]   Determines if the j-axis (y) will be flipped (default=false)
  --flipk [s]   Determines if the k-axis (z) will be flipped (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

gradientimage.oneliner: This algorithm computes image gradients using a 2D/3D Gaussian kernel
gradientimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js gradientimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   Input image
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --sigma [n]   The gaussian kernel standard deviation (either in voxels or mm) (default=1), range=0:8
  --inmm [s]   Determines whether kernel standard deviation (sigma) will be measured in millimeters or voxels (default=true)
  --radiusfactor [n]   This affects the size of the convolution kernel which is computed as sigma*radius+1 (default=2)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

headerinfo.oneliner: Reads the Image Headers of Multiple .nii/.nii.gz images and optionally stores result in a json file
headerinfo.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js headerinfo [options]

Options:
  -o --logoutput [s]   log file
  --detail [n]   detail level (default=0), range=0:2
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

individualizedparcellation.oneliner: Calculates the individualized parcellation starting from an original (group) parcellation
individualizedparcellation.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js individualizedparcellation [options]

Options:
  --fmri <s>   The fMRI image to parcellate
  --parc <s>   The original (group) parcellation to individualize
  -o --output <s>   Output: the individualized parcellation
  --numregions [n]   The number of regions in the original (group) parcellation (default=268), range=1:5000
  --smooth [n]   Kernel size [mm] of FWHM filter size (default=4), range=0:20
  --saveexemplars [s]   Saves exemplars in second frame (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

infomodule.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js infomodule [options]

Options:
  --logoutput [s]   log file
  --detail [n]   detail level (default=1), range=1:5
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

inverttransformation.oneliner: Calculates the inverse transformatio for a given transformation
inverttransformation.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js inverttransformation [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   Load the transformation to invert
  -y --xform2 [s]   The second transformation to combine with first
  -z --xform3 [s]   The third transformation to combine with first and second
  -r --ref [s]   The Reference image (defines the coordinate space)
  -o --output <s>   The output (inverse transformation)
  --lambda [n]   Extra regularization smoothness term weight (default=0.1), range=0:1
  --tolerance [n]   Fitting to tolerance (default=0.001)
  --windowsize [n]   Fitting quality (default=2), range=1:2
  --spacing [n]   The control point spacing of the output grid transform (default=25), range=1:50
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)
  --optimization [s]   Optimization Method (default=ConjugateGradient), values=[HillClimb,GradientDescent,ConjugateGradient]
  --stepsize [n]   Step size for gradient computation (default=0.5), range=0.125:4
  --levels [n]   Number of levels in multiresolution optimization (default=2), range=1:4
  --iterations [n]   Number of iterations (per level and step) (default=20), range=1:32
  --resolution [n]   Factor to reduce the resolution prior to registration (default=2), range=1:5
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)
  --steps [n]   Number of steps in multiresolution optimization (default=1), range=1:4

jacobianimage.oneliner: Calculates the determinant of the jacobian of the transformation for the volume specified by the given image.
jacobianimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js jacobianimage [options]

Options:
  -x --xform <s>   The transformation used to compute the Jacobian Image
  -i --input <s>   Image that defines the size of the Jacobian Image
  -o --output [s]   Jacobian Output Image
  --nonlinearonly [s]   If true removes the average jacobian from the output (default=false)

  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --outmotionmat [s]   The filename for saving the motion matrix
  --outgsrvector [s]   The filename for saving the GSR Signal Matrix
  --outputmask [s]   The filename for saving the Output Mask
  --tr [n]   Temporal resolution of image (in s) (default=1), range=0:8
  --sigma [n]   The gaussian kernel standard deviation (in fwhmax) If <0.01 no smoothing is done (default=0), range=0:8
  --regressmotion [s]   If true regress motion parameters (default=true)
  --motionparams [s]   The filename to load motion parameters from (specify csv or .json. If not specified, try to infer from image filename .nii.gz --> .json) (default=)
  --dobandpass [s]   If true performs bandpass filtering (default=true)
  --dogsr [s]   If true performs bandpass filtering (default=true)
  --polynomial [n]   Polynomial order to regress for drift correction (0=just mean term, -1=ignore) (default=0), range=-1:3
  --blow [n]   Low pass cutoff Hz (default=0.008), range=0.001:5
  --bhigh [n]   High pass cutoff Hz (default=0.2), range=0.001:5
  --threshold [n]   Fractional Threshold to create mask (default=0.1), range=0:0.5
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

preprocessoptical.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js preprocessoptical [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   Load the image to be fixed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --sigma [n]   The gaussian kernel standard deviation (either in voxels) (default=1), range=0:8
  --biascorrect [s]   If true correct for z-stack attenuation (default=true)
  --resample [s]   If true resamples to have isotropic resolution (default=true)
  --factor [n]   Resample to this x z resolution (default=1), range=1:4
  --ras [s]   If true reorient the image to RAS (default=true)
  --normalize [s]   If true normalize intensities (default=true)
  --mask [s]   If true masks background (default=true)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

process4dimage.oneliner: This algorithm computes voxel wise time statistics from a 4D image.
process4dimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js process4dimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --operation [s]   The operation to perform (default=mean), values=[mean,meansigma,rms,max,min]
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

projectaverageimage.oneliner: This algorithm averages a 2D image in a mask and projects the average from a 3D image to a 2D
projectaverageimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js projectaverageimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The image to be projected
  -m --mask <s>   The mask used to average inside
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --flip [s]   It true project along the increasing axis (default=false)
  --axis [s]   Which axis to project along ('x', 'y', 'z', 'auto') (default=y), values=[x,y,z,auto]
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

projectimage.oneliner: This algorithm performs image projection from a 3D image to a 2D image using eigher MIP or shaded projection
projectimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js projectimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The image to be projected
  -m --mask [s]   The mask used to estimate the boundary
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --mode [s]   Mode, mip,project,average (default=mip), values=[mip,project,average]
  --usemask [s]   It true project use the mask (no mip in that case) (default=false)
  --sigma [n]   The gaussian kernel standard deviation (either in voxels or mm) (default=0), range=0:3
  --flip [s]   It true project along the increasing axis (default=false)
  --axis [s]   Which axis to project along ('x', 'y', 'z', 'auto') (default=y), values=[x,y,z,auto]
  --gradsigma [n]   The gaussian kernel standard deviation for gradient computation (in 'project' mode) (default=2), range=0:4
  --threshold [n]   The intensity threshold to detect background in shaded projection (default=1), range=0:100000
  --window [n]   Number of voxels to average in 'average' or 'project' mode (default=3), range=1:10
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

projectresliceimage.oneliner: Project Reslices a 2D optical image via 3D to a new 2D atlas space optical image
projectresliceimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js projectresliceimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   Load the 2D image to projectReslice
  -r --reference <s>   Load the 3D reference image
  -a --angio <s>   Load the 3D angio image
  -x --xform <s>   Load the transformation used to map Atlas to 3D Image of individual mouse
  -y --angioxform <s>   The second transformation used to map 3D Image to 3D optical image of individual mouse
  -z --rotxform <s>   The mapping from projected angio to the optical image
  -o --output <s>   Save the projectResliced image
  -f --ref2d [s]   Save the projected 2D (from ref) image
  --flip [s]   It true project along the increasing axis (default=false)
  --flipy [s]   It true flip the vertical  axis (default=true)
  --axis [s]   Which axis to project along ('x', 'y', 'z', 'auto') (default=y), values=[x,y,z,auto]
  --threshold [n]   The intensity threshold to detect background in shaded projection (default=1), range=0:100000
  --depth [n]   Number of voxels to go below the brain surface (default=1), range=1:10
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

projectreslicemask.oneliner: Reslices and projects a 3D mask to a 2d optical image
projectreslicemask.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js projectreslicemask [options]

Options:
  -r --reference <s>   The 2D optical image to project mask to
  -m --mask <s>   The 3D image or mask (thresholded at 1)
  -a --angio <s>   Load the 3D angio image
  -x --angioxform <s>   Thetransformation used to map 3D Image to 3D optical image of individual mouse
  -y --rotxform <s>   The mapping from projected angio to the optical image
  -o --output <s>   Save the projectResliced mask
  --flip [s]   It true project along the increasing axis (default=false)
  --flipy [s]   It true flip the vertical  axis (default=true)
  --axis [s]   Which axis to project along ('x', 'y', 'z', 'auto') (default=y), values=[x,y,z,auto]
  --threshold [n]   The intensity threshold to detect background in shaded projection (default=1), range=0:100000
  --isobjectmap [s]   If set treat image as object map and do not interpolate (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

quantilenormalizeimage.oneliner: This module will perform quantile normalization on an image. Median=0, Inter-Quartile Range=1
quantilenormalizeimage.help:

  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

regressglobal.oneliner: Regresses the global signal (average) from a time series with the option to specify a weight matrix
regressglobal.help:

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The input data (matrix) to process. Rows=Frames, Columns=Series.
  -w --weight [s]   (Optional). The framewise weight vector
  -o --output <s>   The output matrix
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

regressiontests.help:

Options:
  --logoutput [s]   log file
  --first [n]   The first test to run (0) (default=0), range=0:1000
  --last [n]   The last test to run (-1 = all) (default=-1), range=-1:1000
  --testname [s]   If specified only run tests with this name (default=)

regressout.oneliner: Regresses one time signal from another with the option to specify a weight matrix

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The input data (matrix) to process. Rows=Frames, Columns=Series.
  -w --weight [s]   (Optional). The framewise weight vector
  -r --regressor [s]   The regressor matrix
  -o --output <s>   The output matrix
  --usejs [s]   Use the pure JS implementation of the algorithm (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

regressoutimage.oneliner: Regresses one time signal from another with the option to specify a weight matrix
regressoutimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js regressoutimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -w --weight [s]   (Optional). The framewise weight vector
  -r --regressor [s]   The regressor matrix
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

regularizeobjectmap.oneliner: Performs Objectmap regularization. An objectmap is an image where the values refer to different regions. This modules uses an MRF-based algorithm to smooth the segmentation map. It is similar to a median filter for a binary mask.
regularizeobjectmap.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js regularizeobjectmap [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The binary mask to be regularized
  -o --output <s>   The output mask
  --smoothness [n]   If > 0 then apply spatial regularization MRF model with this value as the weight (default=2), range=1:32
  --convergence [n]   Convergence parameter for the MRF iterations (default=0.2), range=0.01:0.5
  --iterations [n]   Number of MRF iterations (default=8), range=1:20
  --internaliterations [n]   Number of Internal iterations (default=4), range=1:20
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

removematrixcols.oneliner: Takes a matrix and removes a number of rows.
removematrixcols.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js removematrixcols [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The matrix to remove columns from
  -o --output <s>   The matrix without the chosen columns
  --cols [s]   The columns to remove formatted as a series of numbers separated by commas, e.g. 1,2,3. The first row should be 1, the second 2, etc.

reorientimage.oneliner: This algorithm reorients an image to a fixed orientation. The letters refer to the direction towards the individual axes are increasing. RAS, for example, means an image where the first axis goes from left-to-Right, the second axis from posterior-to-Anterior and the third axis from inferior-to-Superior
reorientimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js reorientimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   input
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --logoutput [s]   log file
  --orient [s]   Output image orientation (default=RAS), values=[RAS,LPS,LAS]
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

resampleimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js resampleimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --xsp [n]   Desired voxel spacing in X direction (default=-1)
  --ysp [n]   Desired voxel spacing in Y direction (default=-1)
  --zsp [n]   Desired voxel spacing in Z direction (default=-1)
  --interpolation [n]   Type of interpolation to use (0 = nearest-neighbor, 1 = linear, 3 = cubic) (default=1), values=[0,1,3]
  --backgroundvalue [n]   value to use for outside the region covered by the original image (at the boundaries) (default=0)
  --usejs [s]   Use the pure JS implementation of the algorithm (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

resliceimage.oneliner: Reslices an existing image to match a reference and a transformation
resliceimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js resliceimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   Load the image to reslice
  -r --reference [s]   Load the reference image (if not specified use input)
  -x --xform <s>   Load the transformation used to reslice the image
  -y --xform2 [s]   The second transformation to combine with first
  -z --xform3 [s]   The third transformation to combine with first and second
  -o --output [s]   Save the resliced image
  --interpolation [n]   Which type of interpolation to use (3 = cubic, 1 = linear, 0 = nearest-neighbor) (default=1), values=[0,1,3]
  --forcefloat [s]   If true, force output to float (default=false)
  --backgroundvalue [n]   Value to use for outside the image (default=0)
  --addgrid [s]   If true, adds a grid overlay to the image to visualize the effect of the transformation(s) (default=false)
  --gridgap [n]   If add grid is true this controls the grid spacing (default=8)
  --gridvalue [n]   If add grid is true this controls the intensity of the grid (as a function of the maximum image intensity) (default=0.5)

  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --zscore [s]   Convert correlations to z-score. (default=true)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

segmentimage.oneliner: Performs image segmentation using a histogram-based method if smoothness = 0.0 or using plus mrf segmentation if smoothness > 0.0
segmentimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js segmentimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --numclasses [n]   Number of classes to segment image into (default=3), range=2:8
  --maxsigmaratio [n]   Enforced ratio between minimum and maximum standard deviation between class parameters (default=0.2), range=0:1
  --robust [s]   Use robust range algorithm to eliminate outliers prior to segmentation (default=false)
  --numbins [n]   Number of bins in the histogram (default=256), range=32:1024
  --smoothhisto [s]   Whether or not to apply smoothing to the histogram (default=true)
  --smoothness [n]   If > 0 then apply spatial regularization MRF model with this value as the weight (default=0), range=0:100
  --mrfconvergence [n]   Convergence parameter for the MRF iterations (default=0.2), range=0.01:0.5
  --mrfiterations [n]   Number of MRF iterations (default=8), range=1:20
  --internaliterations [n]   Number of internal iterations (default=4), range=1:20
  --noisesigma2 [n]   Estimate of the standard deviation of noise in the image. This is used to add robustness to the algorithm (default=0), range=0:1000
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

shiftscaleimage.oneliner: This element will shift and scale an image and cast to desired output. E.g. out=(input+shift)*scale
shiftscaleimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js shiftscaleimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --shift [n]   The Shift value to add to all voxels (default=0), range=-10000.1:10000.1
  --scale [n]   The Scale to multiple all voxels after the shift value is applied (default=1), range=-10000.1:10000.1
  --outtype [s]   Output Type (default=Same), values=[Same,UChar,Short,Int,Float,Double]
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

slicebiascorrect.oneliner: Performs slice-based intensity inhomogeneity (bias field) correction on an image to correct for acquisition artifacts. This includes B1 inhomogeneity correction for MRI, or attenuation issues in microscopy.
slicebiascorrect.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js slicebiascorrect [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --axis [s]   Which axis to correct along ('x', 'y', 'z', 'triple') (default=z), values=[x,y,z,triple]
  --threshold [n]   This sets the threshold (percentage of max intensity), below which the image is masked (default=0.05), range=0:0.5
  --returnbiasfield [s]   If false (default), this returns the the corrected image. Otherwise (true) it returns the estimated bias field. (default=false)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

smoothimage.oneliner: This algorithm performs image smoothing using a 2D/3D Gaussian kernel
smoothimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js smoothimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   input
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --sigma [n]   The gaussian kernel standard deviation (either in voxels or mm) (default=1), range=0:8
  --inmm [s]   Determines whether kernel standard deviation (sigma) will be measured in millimeters or voxels (default=true)
  --fwhmax [s]   If true treat kernel in units of full-width-at-half max (FWHM) (not as the actual value of the sigma in the gaussian filter.) (default=false)
  --usejs [s]   Use the pure JS implementation of the algorithm (default=false)
  --vtkboundary [s]   If true mimic how VTK handles boundary conditions for smoothing (instead of tiling default) (default=false)
  --radiusfactor [n]   This affects the size of the convolution kernel which is computed as sigma*radius+1 (default=2)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

splitimageintoframes.oneliner: Splits a Single 4D Image into frames
splitimageintoframes.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js splitimageintoframes [options]

  -i --input <s>   input
  --outputstem [s]   Output filename stem (default=)
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)

Usage: node bisweb.js stackimages [options]

  -o --output <s>   The stackd image

thresholdimage.oneliner: This element will threshold an image -- values between the thresholds will be considered 'input' and values outside will be considered 'out'
thresholdimage.help:
Usage: node bisweb.js thresholdimage [options]

Options:
  -i --input <s>   The filename for the image to be processed
  -o --output <s>   The output image filename
  --low [n]   The threshold below which values will be classified as 'out' (default=1)
  --high [n]   The value above which values will be classified as 'out' (default=2)
  --replacein [s]   If true, values classified as 'in' will be replaced by 'in value' (default=false)
  --replaceout [s]   If true, values classified as 'out' will be replaced by 'out value' (default=true)
  --inval [n]   Value to replace 'in' values with, -1 is mapped to the maximum value in the image (default=1), values=[0,1,100,-1]
  --outval [n]   Value to replace 'out' values with, -1 is mapped to the minimum value in the image (default=0), values=[0,1,100,-1]
  --saturate [s]   If true then if > threshold saturate to threshold instead of out value (default=false)
  --outtype [s]   Output Type (default=Same), values=[Same,UChar,Short]
  --debug [s]   Toggles debug logging (default=false)
